hook.convey: a bill or a score is many small amounts joined by operations → one line of numbers and signs that stands for the total = an expression; cricket runs from fours and sixes, a kitchen shopping list

use.hi: Cricket mein ek batsman ne 3 chauke aur 2 chhakke maare. Uske run ko ek line mein likh sakte ho: 3 × 4 + 2 × 6. Yeh line hi ek expression hai.
use.en: In cricket a batsman hit 3 fours and 2 sixes. You can write his runs in one line: 3 × 4 + 2 × 6. That line is an expression.

use.hi: Kitchen ke liye 2 packet atta aur 5 packet maggi lene hain. Har cheez ka daam guna se aur poora bill jod se ek hi expression mein aa jaata hai.
use.en: For the kitchen you need 2 packets of flour and 5 packets of maggi. Each item's cost by multiplying, and the whole bill by adding, fit into one expression.

explain.convey: expression = numbers joined by operations that stands for a value; bill: 3 samosas at ₹15 and 2 chai at ₹10 → each item = count × price → join with + → 3 × 15 + 2 × 10

point.hi: Ek stall par 3 samose ₹15 wale liye, toh unka daam 3 × 15. Saath mein 2 chai ₹10 wali, toh 2 × 10. Dono ko jodo, toh poora bill: 3 × 15 + 2 × 10. Numbers aur chinh milkar ek value batate hain, isi ko expression kehte hain.
point.en: At a stall, 3 samosas at ₹15 each were bought, so their cost is 3 × 15. With them, 2 chai at ₹10 each, so 2 × 10. Join the two and the whole bill is 3 × 15 + 2 × 10. Numbers and signs together stand for one value; that is called an expression.

prompt.hi: Agle din isi stall par 4 samose aur 3 chai li, daam wahi. Us din ke bill ka expression kya hoga?
prompt.en: The next day 4 samosas and 3 chai were bought at the same stall, same prices. What is the expression for that day's bill?

explain.convey: '7 less than 30' → find what it is less than (30) = the start → take 7 away → 30 − 7; the words say 7 first, the expression starts with 30

point.hi: '30 se 7 kam' mein pehle dekho ki kis number se kam hai: 30 se. Shuru wahi number hai, aur usmein se 7 ghatate hain: 30 − 7. Angrezi mein 7 pehle bolte hain, par expression 30 se shuru hota hai.
point.en: In '7 less than 30', first see what it is less than: 30. That number is the start, and 7 is taken away from it: 30 − 7. In English the 7 is said first, but the expression starts with 30.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah, '45 se 9 kam' ka expression kya hai?
prompt.en: In the same way, what is the expression for '9 less than 45'?

explain.convey: a total shared equally → add first, then divide → the part done first goes in brackets: (300 + 60) ÷ 4; pizza ₹300 and cold drink ₹60 shared by 4 friends

point.hi: 4 dost ₹300 ka pizza aur ₹60 ki cold drink ka kharcha barabar baant-te hain. Pehle poora kharcha jodna hai, phir use 4 mein baantna hai. Jo kaam pehle hota hai, use bracket mein likhte hain: (300 + 60) ÷ 4.
point.en: 4 friends share the cost of a ₹300 pizza and a ₹60 cold drink equally. First the whole cost is added, then it is divided by 4. The part done first goes in brackets: (300 + 60) ÷ 4.

prompt.hi: Is expression ki value nikaalo: har dost ka hissa kitne rupaye ka hai?
prompt.en: Find the value of this expression: how many rupees is each friend's share?

problem.hi: Raju 2 kg chawal ₹55 kilo ke bhaav se aur biscuit ke 3 packet ₹20 wale khareedta hai. Woh ₹500 ka note deta hai. Use wapas milne wale paison ka expression likho aur uski value nikaalo.
problem.en: Raju buys 2 kg of rice at ₹55 per kg and 3 packets of biscuits at ₹20 each. He pays with a ₹500 note. Write an expression for the change he gets, and find its value.

givens.en: 2 kg of rice at ₹55 per kg

find.hi: wapas milne wale paison ka expression aur uski value
find.en: an expression for the change, and its value

do.en: Write the cost of the rice

why.hi: 2 kilo hain aur har kilo ₹55 ka hai
why.en: there are 2 kg and each kg costs ₹55

do.en: Write the cost of the biscuits

why.hi: 3 packet hain aur har packet ₹20 ka hai
why.en: there are 3 packets and each costs ₹20

do.hi: Poore bill ko bracket mein rakhkar ₹500 mein se ghatao
do.en: Put the whole bill in brackets and take it away from ₹500

why.hi: wapas wahi milta hai jo poora bill dene ke baad bachta hai
why.en: the change is what remains after the whole bill is paid

do.hi: Bracket ke andar ka bill nikaalo
do.en: Work out the bill inside the brackets

prompt.hi: Ab ₹500 mein se poora bill ₹170 ghatao. Raju ko kitne rupaye wapas milenge?
prompt.en: Now take the whole bill of ₹170 away from ₹500. How many rupees does Raju get back?

answer.hi: expression 500 − (2 × 55 + 3 × 20) hai, aur Raju ko ₹330 wapas milenge
answer.en: the expression is 500 − (2 × 55 + 3 × 20), and Raju gets ₹330 back

why.hi: pehle har cheez ka daam guna se bana, phir poora bill jod se, aur bracket ne poore bill ko ek saath ₹500 mein se ghataya
why.en: each item's cost came from multiplying, the whole bill from adding, and the brackets took the whole bill away from ₹500 at once

prompt.hi: Ek number 90 se 14 kam hai. Us number ka expression likho.
prompt.en: A number is 14 less than 90. Write an expression for that number.

prompt.hi: Sohan ke paas ₹1000 the. Usne ₹120 wali 4 tickets khareedi. Bache hue paison ka expression likho.
prompt.en: Sohan had ₹1000. He bought 4 tickets at ₹120 each. Write an expression for the money left.

ladder.why: first straight bill: two items, count × price each, joined by +
'12 less than 40' → start at 40, the order-of-words trap on its own
money left after buying: start amount − count × price
auto fare: a first-km charge plus 6 more km, the child finds the 6 first
pool, a group fee, then sharing: brackets around the part done first

remediation.move: act the phrase on a number line: find what it is less than → put the dot there (the start) → jump back the other number; the start is written first

say.hi: '40 se 9 kam' mein dot pehle 40 par rakho, kyunki kam 40 se hona hai. Phir 9 peeche jump karo. Jahan se shuru kiya, wahi expression mein pehle aata hai: 40 − 9.
say.en: For '9 less than 40', put the dot on 40 first, because it is 40 that becomes less. Then jump 9 back. Where you started comes first in the expression: 40 − 9.

prompt.hi: Shabd hain '75 se 8 kam'. Inka expression likho.
prompt.en: The words are '8 less than 75'. Write their expression.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab expression likhna aa gaya. Agle hisse mein do expressions ki tulna karenge, bina poora calculate kiye, sirf unke hisse dekhkar.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you can write an expression. In the next part we will compare two expressions without working them out fully, just by looking at their parts.

hook.convey: two totals made of parts → look at how each part changed instead of adding; one part up and the other down by the same amount → same total; taking away more from the same start → less left; two batsmen's runs, coins spent in a game

use.hi: Cricket match mein ek batsman ne do innings mein 23 aur 48 run banaye, doosre ne 24 aur 47. Kisne zyada banaye, yeh bina jode bhi pata chal sakta hai.
use.en: In a cricket match one batsman scored 23 and 48 runs in two innings, another scored 24 and 47. Who scored more can be found without adding.

use.hi: Game mein tumhare paas 1000 coins hain. Ek level par 345 coins kharch ho sakte hain, doosre par 354. Kahan zyada coins bachenge, yeh ghataye bina socha ja sakta hai.
use.en: In a game you have 1000 coins. One level could cost 345 coins, another 354. Where more coins are left can be worked out without subtracting.

explain.convey: 23 + 48 vs 24 + 47 → part by part: 23 → 24 is up 1, 48 → 47 is down 1 → the +1 and −1 cancel → same total, no adding needed

point.hi: Dono ke hisse milao. Pehla hissa 23 se 24 hua, yaani 1 badha. Doosra hissa 48 se 47 hua, yaani 1 ghata.
point.en: Match the parts of the two. The first part went from 23 to 24, so it is up by 1. The second part went from 48 to 47, so it is down by 1.

prompt.hi: Toh bina jode batao: 23 + 48 aur 24 + 47 mein kaun bada hai, ya dono barabar hain?
prompt.en: So without adding, which is bigger, 23 + 48 or 24 + 47, or are they equal?

explain.convey: 100 − 37 vs 100 − 29 → same start 100 → which takes away more → taking away more leaves less; a box of 100 toffees, 37 taken out once, 29 another time

point.hi: Dono mein shuru 100 se hai, jaise 100 toffee ka ek dabba. Pehle mein dabbe se 37 toffee nikaali, doosre mein 29 toffee nikaali.
point.en: Both start at 100, like a box of 100 toffees. In the first, 37 toffees are taken out of the box; in the second, 29 are taken out.

prompt.hi: Bina ghataye batao: dabbe mein zyada toffee kab bachengi, pehle mein ya doosre mein?
prompt.en: Without subtracting, when are more toffees left in the box, in the first or in the second?

problem.hi: Bina jode batao: 247 + 389 aur 250 + 386 mein kaun bada hai, ya dono barabar hain?
problem.en: Without adding, compare 247 + 389 and 250 + 386: which is bigger, or are they equal?

find.hi: kaun bada hai, bina poora jode
find.en: which is bigger, without adding fully

do.en: Now match the second parts, 389 and 386

prompt.hi: Ek hissa 3 badha aur doosra 3 ghata. Toh 247 + 389 aur 250 + 386 mein kaun bada hai, ya dono barabar hain?
prompt.en: One part went up by 3 and the other went down by 3. So which is bigger, 247 + 389 or 250 + 386, or are they equal?

why.hi: jitna ek hissa badha, utna hi doosra hissa ghata, isliye jod wahi raha
why.en: one part went up by exactly as much as the other went down, so the total stayed the same

prompt.hi: Pehla 486 + 239 hai, doosra 485 + 240. Bina jode batao: kaun bada hai, ya dono barabar hain?
prompt.en: The first is 486 + 239, the second 485 + 240. Without adding: which is bigger, or are they equal?

prompt.hi: Pehla 500 − 168 hai, doosra 500 − 186. Bina ghataye batao, kismein zyada bachta hai: pehle mein ya doosre mein?
prompt.en: The first is 500 − 168, the second 500 − 186. Without subtracting, which leaves more: the first or the second?

prompt.hi: Pehla 73 + 45 hai, doosra 75 + 42. Bina jode batao, kaun bada hai: pehla ya doosra?
prompt.en: The first is 73 + 45, the second 75 + 42. Without adding, which is bigger: the first or the second?

ladder.why: predict first: one part up 1, the other down 1, then check by adding
same start 1000, take away 345 or 354 → taking away more leaves less
products: split 64 × 11 and 65 × 10 into 640 and a bit, compare the bits
why 25 × 18 = 50 × 9: double one factor, halve the other

remediation.move: bar split into two matching parts: move one small block from one part to the other → the whole bar does not change → totals compared by the parts, not by adding

say.hi: Ek patti socho: pehle uske do hisse 50 aur 30 hain. 30 wale hisse se 1 tukda uthakar 50 wale mein rakh do, toh baad mein hisse 51 aur 29 hain. Tukda sirf ek hisse se doosre mein gaya, poori patti utni hi lambi rahi.
say.en: Picture a strip: at first its two parts are 50 and 30. Take 1 block from the 30 part and put it in the 50 part; afterwards the parts are 51 and 29. The block only moved from one part to the other; the whole strip stayed just as long.

prompt.hi: Pehla 68 + 17 hai, doosra 70 + 15. Bina jode batao: kaun bada hai, ya dono barabar hain?
prompt.en: The first is 68 + 17, the second 70 + 15. Without adding: which is bigger, or are they equal?

remediation.move: two equal bars of 200 → take 58 off one and 49 off the other → compare what is left; the bigger piece taken off leaves the shorter leftover

say.hi: Do jebon mein ₹200 hain. Ek jeb se ₹58 nikle, doosri se ₹49. Pehli jeb se zyada nikla, isliye usmein kam bacha: 200 − 58 chhota hai.
say.en: Two pockets have ₹200 each. ₹58 came out of one, ₹49 out of the other. More came out of the first pocket, so less is left in it: 200 − 58 is smaller.

prompt.hi: Pehla 80 − 19 hai, doosra 80 − 12. Bina ghataye batao, kismein zyada bachta hai: pehle mein ya doosre mein?
prompt.en: The first is 80 − 19, the second 80 − 12. Without subtracting, which leaves more: the first or the second?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab expressions ko unke hisse dekhkar compare karna aa gaya. Agle hisse mein ulta karenge: expression diya hoga, aur tum uski kahani banaoge.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you can compare expressions by looking at their parts. In the next part we go the other way: you get an expression and make up its story.

hook.convey: an expression → a story whose events follow its grouping: a × part is one block (so many of the same thing), a bracket is done first; sixes in cricket, packets in a kitchen

use.hi: Expression 4 × 6 + 10 ki ek cricket kahani: ek batsman ne 4 sixer maare aur baaki 10 run daud kar banaye. 4 × 6 ek hi cheez hai, chhakkon ke run.
use.en: A cricket story for 4 × 6 + 10: a batsman hit 4 sixes and ran the other 10 runs. 4 × 6 is one thing, the runs from sixes.

use.hi: Kitchen ke liye ₹25 wale 3 packet maggi aur ₹40 ka ek packet doodh liya: yeh 3 × 25 + 40 ki kahani hai.
use.en: For the kitchen, 3 packets of maggi at ₹25 and one ₹40 packet of milk were bought: that is a story for 3 × 25 + 40.

explain.convey: 50 + 4 × 10 → the × part is one block, four ₹10 notes, named first → the story joins ₹50 and that block; not 'add 4, then 10 times'

point.hi: 50 + 4 × 10 mein 4 × 10 ek block hai, yaani ₹10 ke 4 note. Toh kahani yeh hai: kisi ke paas ₹50 the, phir use ₹10 ke 4 note mile.
point.en: In 50 + 4 × 10, 4 × 10 is one block: four ₹10 notes. So the story is: someone had ₹50, then got four ₹10 notes.

prompt.hi: Is kahani mein aakhir mein kitne rupaye hain?
prompt.en: In this story, how many rupees are there at the end?

explain.convey: 200 − 4 × 30 → two stories on the board: A takes four ₹30 books away from ₹200 (the × block taken away), B spends ₹4 and then makes the money 30 times (left to right) → only A follows the grouping

point.hi: Board par expression 200 − 4 × 30 ke liye do kahaniyan hain. Kahani A mein ₹200 the aur ₹30 wali 4 kitaab li. Kahani B mein ₹200 the, ₹4 kharch kiye, phir bache paise 30 guna ho gaye.
point.en: The board has two stories for the expression 200 − 4 × 30. In story A, there was ₹200 and 4 books at ₹30 were bought. In story B, there was ₹200, ₹4 was spent, then the money left became 30 times as much.

prompt.hi: Kaunsi kahani 200 − 4 × 30 se match karti hai, A ya B?
prompt.en: Which story matches 200 − 4 × 30, A or B?

problem.hi: Expression (180 − 20) ÷ 4 se match karti ek chhoti kahani banao, aur uski value nikaalo.
problem.en: Make up a short story that matches the expression (180 − 20) ÷ 4, and find its value.

find.hi: ek matching kahani aur expression ki value
find.en: a matching story and the expression's value

why.hi: bracket wala kaam sabse pehle hota hai

steps.result: bache hue 160 ko 4 mein barabar baanto

why.hi: ÷ 4 poore bracket par lagta hai, sirf 20 par nahi
why.en: ÷ 4 applies to the whole bracket, not just to 20

do.en: Fit a story to this shape

steps.result: Dadi ne 4 cousins ko ₹180 diye, unhone milkar ₹20 ki ek patang li aur baaki paise barabar baant liye

why.hi: kahani mein pehle milkar kharcha hai aur phir baantna, bilkul bracket ke order mein
why.en: the story has the shared spending first and then the sharing, in the bracket's order

prompt.hi: Is kahani mein har cousin ko kitne rupaye milenge?
prompt.en: In this story, how many rupees does each cousin get?

answer.hi: Dadi ne 4 cousins ko ₹180 diye, unhone ₹20 ki patang milkar li aur baaki barabar baanta, har cousin ko ₹40 mile
answer.en: Dadi gave ₹180 to 4 cousins; they bought a ₹20 kite together and shared the rest equally, so each cousin got ₹40

why.hi: kahani pehle bracket wala kaam karti hai, 180 − 20, aur phir sirf bache hue 160 ko 4 mein baant-ti hai
why.en: the story does the bracket first, 180 − 20, and then shares only the remaining 160 among 4

prompt.hi: Kaunsi kahani 30 + 5 × 8 se match karti hai? Kahani A: ₹30 the, phir ₹8 wale 5 pen mile. Kahani B: ₹30 the, ₹5 aur mile, phir paise 8 guna ho gaye. A ya B?
prompt.en: Which story matches 30 + 5 × 8? Story A: there was ₹30, then 5 pens worth ₹8 each were received. Story B: there was ₹30, ₹5 more came, then the money became 8 times as much. A or B?

prompt.hi: Expression 120 − 4 × 15 ki kahani: ₹120 the, aur ₹15 wali 4 copy khareedi. Kitne rupaye bache?
prompt.en: A story for the expression 120 − 4 × 15: there was ₹120, and 4 notebooks at ₹15 each were bought. How many rupees are left?

ladder.why: choose between two stories for 100 − 3 × 20: the × block is taken away as one piece
tell a shopping story for 5 × 12 + 20 in the child's own words
three stories for (240 − 3 × 40) ÷ 4: bracket and × block together

remediation.move: box the × part first → name it as one quantity (three ₹5 coins = one heap) → the story joins the start and that heap → the signs are not read one by one as events

say.hi: 40 + 3 × 5 mein 3 × 5 ko pehle ek block maano: ₹5 ke 3 sikke, ek dher. Kahani yeh banti hai: ₹40 the, aur ₹5 ke 3 sikke mile.
say.en: In 40 + 3 × 5, treat 3 × 5 as one block first: three ₹5 coins, one heap. The story becomes: there was ₹40, and three ₹5 coins came in.

prompt.hi: 25 + 6 × 10 ki kahani: ₹25 the, phir ₹10 ke 6 note mile. Ab kitne rupaye hain?
prompt.en: A story for 25 + 6 × 10: there was ₹25, then six ₹10 notes came in. How many rupees are there now?
